newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi sees Italy inflation falling, warns on euro.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi sees Italy inflation falling, warns on euro.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Wednesday that he expected the inflation rate to keep falling from its current levels.

He also told a hearing in the Senate that it would be wrong to launch a single European currency comprising only Germany and a few other countries, and vowed that Italy would achieve and sustain a key deficit-GDP goal in time for the single currency.
"We are at 2.4 percent (inflation) and we will fall further," Ciampi told a finance and treasury committee hearing on economic and monetary union.
He cautioned that it would be "a political error" and unbalanced to launch EMU with just a small group of members.
"I agree that only countries which bring stability should enter the euro but I'm against the idea that the single currency should comprise few currencies apart from the mark," he said.

Italy is due to draw up a mini-budget within weeks to try to correct a deficit overshoot and qualify for EMU on time. "As regards the deficit-GDP ratio, the three percent (EMU goal) is reachable and sustainable in time," Ciampi said.
